entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] The whisper of 12. The autumn season has arrived; an autumn that breathes with…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

The whisper of 12. The autumn season has arrived; an autumn that breathes with the blowing of its winds and the turning of its trees' leaves from green to yellow. The month of Mehr is bound to the name and memory of three luminous stars in the sky of Iranian culture and art; cherished souls whose long and deep companionship over the past three decades has polished my soul and gladdened my days: Hafez Shirazi, Sohrab Sepehri, and Mohammadreza Shajarian. Shajarian and Sepehri were born in the month of Mehr. The anniversary commemorating the thinking recluse of Shiraz also falls in this month. I am glad that the lecture series "In the Presence of Hafez" begins the day after tomorrow, in the month of Mehr. In this lecture series, I intend to offer my own re-reading and re-creation of thirty ghazals from the Divan of Hafez and to narrate my roughly forty years of familiarity and intimacy with Hafez's life-world here and now. The opening verse of the first ghazal I have chosen for re-reading and narrative-making is as follows: "If the Sufi drinks wine in measure, may it be sweet to him / Otherwise, may he forget the thought of this affair." Other exquisite verses are also found in this ghazal: "Our elder said no error befell the pen of creation / Bravo to his pure vision that covers errors!" and "The King of Turks listens to the words of claimants / May he be ashamed of the injustice done to the sweet Siyavash!" I have repeatedly read the verses of this stunning artistic work of Hafez over the past decades and have gazed upon them and into them. In this process and in the long future ahead, it is as though both I was reading the ghazal and the ghazal was reading me. For this reason, my present understanding of "pure vision that covers errors" and "shame from the injustice of Siyavash's blood" has noticeably changed. This epistemic transformation can also be explained in the language of Gadamerian hermeneutics and by borrowing the doctrine of the "fusion of horizons." It is obvious that Khwajeh Shams al-Din Mohammad Hafez composed his ghazals seven hundred years ago and read his story into the ear of history. You and I, who are today the audience of these poems, belong to a different context, time, and historical horizon. But this does not prevent the important matter that we strive to the best of our ability, in the light of our lived experience here and now, to become the "audience" of these poems and to understand them; an address that takes place in today's horizon and is the product of our creative and methodical encounter with the text. Of course, in this kind of dialectical encounter with the text, the beliefs, values, attitudes, and the "soul" and "world" of you and me, which have changed over time, pour forth, play an important role in the "process" of addressing the text, and create novel "products" and place them before others." Quoted from the book: "Velvety Whispers," Volume Two. Author: Soroush Dabbagh https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdrpVwpKf7D/?stkn=MmJlbnc2dGV1d284

Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

Dear esteemed Dr. Soroush Dabbagh, greetings. Sir, I am a veteran of the Iran-Iraq war, and I had the honor of being a student of your honorable father in the Methodology course during my master's degree in Sociology at Allameh University. Unfortunately, in the 2010s my illness worsened and I was hospitalized many times in neuropsychiatric hospitals. After 2021, when I retired, I spend my time with lecture series and studying philosophy, from Dr. Ardabili to the late Mohammad Ali Moradi and many others. Fortunately, for some time now I have become acquainted with your lecture series. Despite the site being filtered..., I have downloaded your lecture series through every hardship and follow your delightful discussions, especially in Western philosophy. Unfortunately, your lecture series on Schopenhauer, Hume, Descartes, Russell, and Heidegger are not accessible. I request that you guide me.

__Greetings dear..., honorable sir, thank you for your affectionate message. First, let me say that I, like many Iranians, will remain indebted for the rest of my life to the bravery, sincerity, courage, and selflessness of you soldiers of this land during the eight-year war; had you not been there and not sacrificed your lives, health, and comfort, it is not clear what situation we would be in now. From afar, I kiss your hands, I am grateful to you, and in the words of Hafez I say to you:

"Never will your image fade from the tablet of my heart and soul
Never will that graceful cypress depart from my memory"

And:
"Upon this turquoise arc they have written in gold
That nothing but the goodness of the generous shall endure"

Secondly, I am truly delighted that my oral works and lecture series have been of use to you in these difficult times and that you have found them beneficial. You can download the audio files of the aforementioned lecture series and possibly my other lecture series through my website and Telegram channel, the links of which I am providing for you. You can also download them from the Telegram channel "Soroush Archive," which has been established through the efforts of a dear unseen friend.

soroushdabagh.com
https://t.me/Soroushdabbagh_Official

With affection and respect
Soroush Dabbagh

Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

Fortunately, the technical work on my latest book and spiritual child, "Narratives of Suffering and War," is nearing completion. I hope it will be published in the first half of Mehr and made available to those interested. Passages from the book's introduction are as follows: "Over the past fifteen months, tremendous and strange events have befallen this land and nation; events the likes of even one of which many people living in Europe, Australia, and North America do not experience in their lifetime. Two devastating wars that began with the blatant aggression of Israel and America against our country's soil, and whose aftershocks are still ongoing and have severely affected the security and livelihood of millions of Iranians. Tragically, more than four thousand of my and your compatriots have been drenched in their own blood during these two wars, including the innocent elementary school students of the 'Shajarat Tayyebah' school in Minab County. In addition, the horrific events that occurred after last Dey's protests and in the interval between the two wars, which took the lives of more than three thousand protesting and desperate citizens and cast their lifeless bodies upon the soil. In the midst of this, many families were bereaved, distraught, and destroyed, and they still remain in shock, mourning, and sorrow. Tragically, the ongoing sorrowful tale of the executions of Dey's protesters has added to the volume of these calamities. The psyche of many citizens has been wounded and afflicted during this period, and their wounds still bleed. The storm of events has made the atmosphere extremely dusty, and many people, with an abundance of fear and worry, are monitoring news filled with ambiguity, hoping that through the thought, judgment, and prudence of a few of the rulers, they might 'tunnel toward the light' and imagine a better future. The writer of these lines, although by the decree of fate has resided in North America for years and spends days and nights in this geographical region; yet his heart and soul are deeply bound to that soil and water and beat with longing for its prosperity and elevation, for 'my lamp burns in this house, my water is drunk from the jug of this Ayaz, and my bread is on this table'... Now that the waters have somewhat settled and the dust has subsided, I give thanks to the soul of the world that in those days when 'stones were raining down from the catapult of the heavens' and a heavy atmosphere prevailed, especially outside the country, and openly opposing the war was not an easy task; I did not become captive to the 'dictatorship of the atmosphere' and was not subjugated by the praise and blame of Amr and Zayd, I did not deviate from my national and ethical principles, and I defended the territorial integrity of Iran and the soil and water and my country. Despite all the minor and major criticisms I have had and continue to have regarding the country's mode of political governance...👇👇👇 https://www.instagram.com/p/DdZy_pMKrMh/?stkn=MTVpcWk3MXduMTU3bw==

Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

"Never shall your image depart from the tablet of my heart and soul,
Never shall that graceful cypress depart from my memory.
Whatever burden of grief for you rests upon my wretched heart,
It may depart from my heart, but that one shall never depart from my heart."

On the arrival of the fourth anniversary of the passing of the dear Mahsa Amini and all those killed in the progressive and blessed movement "Woman, Life, Freedom" — a movement that, though suppressed, had lasting achievements and imposed itself upon the rulers, forcing them to accept the colorful lifestyles of citizens....

The written account and the collection of my writings during the days of the "Mahsa Movement" have been recorded in a chapter of the book "The Untrodden Path: Essays on Politics, Religion, and Society," read to the ear of history, and placed before audiences and those interested. In hope of the arrival of a bright tomorrow — a tomorrow in which economic and psychological security, freedom, social justice, and fundamental citizenship rights are institutionalized in our beloved country, and our sorrowful and suffering people no longer pass their nights and days and "still" in longing to obtain and taste them:

"Someday we will find our doves again
And kindness will take the hand of beauty
A day when the least song
Is a kiss
And every human being
For every human being
Is a brother...
A day when you come, when you come forever
And kindness becomes one with beauty
A day when we again scatter seeds for our doves, and I await that day
Even a day when I no longer exist"
